goal.summary: Replace the consistently unavailable npm registry audit endpoint with a dedicated, fail-closed OSV lockfile audit that can complete reliably and preserve downstream exact-SHA adapter verification.
deliverables: checksum-pinned scanner and generation-bound advisory database
dedicated stable Dependency audit CI job
one complete exact-SHA green CI run
constraints: Do not use the npm registry security audit endpoint in CI
Do not report success when the scanner, database, either lockfile, or scan evidence is missing or invalid
Fail on every OSV finding; document that this is a non-equivalent replacement for pnpm audit --audit-level=high
Use only checksum-pinned executable bytes and generation-bound database bytes
Keep CI permissions at contents: read and use no credentials
Keep Frozen install, Repository gates, and Adapter integrations check names stable
Preserve Adapter integrations fail-closed dependency behavior
Do not cache stale vulnerability data as a successful fallback
exclusions: dependency upgrades unrelated to an actual finding
production credentials or private advisory sources

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: Replace, rather than retry, the npm audit endpoint in CI.
assumptionsAndDecisions.evidence: Three bounded attempts consistently failed against the same endpoint in run 33833838983.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: Use a checksum-pinned OSV-Scanner binary and a fresh generation-specific offline npm database download.
assumptionsAndDecisions.evidence: OSV v2.3.8 supports pnpm lockfiles and official offline scanning; the release API publishes the reviewed binary digest.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: Fail on every OSV finding and describe the replacement as non-equivalent, not as strict parity with pnpm audit --audit-level=high.
assumptionsAndDecisions.evidence: OSV v2.3.8 has no minimum-severity flag and uses a different advisory model; filtering unknown or producer-specific severity would create ambiguity.

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: Use a repository-owned verifier instead of the tagged OSV reusable workflow.

rdRecord.question: Why did bounded pnpm audit retries fail?
rdRecord.method: Read-only repository and GitHub Actions log inspection.
rdRecord.isolation: No writes or workflow mutations; repository remained clean.
rdRecord.observation: All three attempts reached ERR_SOCKET_TIMEOUT against the npm quick-audit POST endpoint and exited 124.
rdRecord.planImplication: Remove this endpoint from the CI critical path rather than increasing retries.

rdRecord.question: Can OSV scan this repository without the npm audit endpoint?
rdRecord.method: Current OSV documentation, v2.3.8 release metadata/source, and parallel read-only research retrieved 2026-09-04.
rdRecord.isolation: Read-only web retrieval and repository inspection; no binaries, databases, containers, or workflows executed.
rdRecord.observation: OSV supports pnpm-lock.yaml, explicit repeated lockfiles, offline npm database scans, JSON output, all-package output, and documented status codes. Linux amd64 v2.3.8 has SHA256 bc98e15319ed0d515e3f9235287ba53cdc5535d576d24fd573978ecfe9ab92dc.
rdRecord.planImplication: Use a pinned binary, generation-bound database, explicit lockfiles, and repository-owned adjudication.

rdRecord.question: What false-green paths must be closed?
rdRecord.method: Hostile independent critique of OSV v2.3.8 offline behavior and the proposed CI topology.
rdRecord.isolation: Read-only source and documentation review; no repository or external mutation.
rdRecord.observation: The scanner can skip malformed local database entries, repository config can ignore findings, combined output can omit a lockfile without independent validation, and the tagged reusable workflow can mishandle missing scan results.
rdRecord.planImplication: Validate database transfer/archive, override config, require exact per-lockfile source/package evidence, adjudicate status/report consistency, and own artifact handling.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Use OSV-Scanner v2.3.8 Linux amd64 bytes only after matching hard-coded SHA256 and expected byte size; assert reported version before scanning.
Database metadata maximum age is 48 hours, maximum future clock skew is 5 minutes, and metadata name, content type, generation, updated timestamp, size, and MD5 are mandatory.
discoveredRequirements.source: Local fail-closed policy based on OSV offline and GCS generation APIs; OSV publishes no freshness SLA.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Download the exact GCS generation, stream to a temporary file, enforce metadata size plus a 350 MiB hard cap, validate MD5 and ZIP integrity, then atomically publish under runner temp.
discoveredRequirements.source: GCS generation/checksum guidance and independent critique.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Use a trusted empty config outside the checkout and explicit canonical paths for exactly pnpm-lock.yaml and csm-browse/pnpm-lock.yaml.
Use --offline --all-vulns --all-packages and JSON output; fail on any Warning line for pinned v2.3.8, any non-0/1 scanner status, or any status/report/coverage mismatch.
discoveredRequirements.source: OSV v2.3.8 flags/output source and hostile critique.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Metadata requests use 15-second attempts, binary requests 60-second attempts, database body requests 90-second attempts, each with at most three attempts and bounded backoff; scanner timeout is 240 seconds and job timeout is 15 minutes (worst-case total stays under the job cap). Response bodies are downloaded inside the retry loop so truncated transfers retry.
discoveredRequirements.source: Local operability policy resolving critique finding on unbounded response bodies.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Always upload bounded report, redacted stderr, scanner status, and database provenance; never upload the database or executable.
discoveredRequirements.source: Independent critique and existing repository diagnostic-artifact pattern.

design.summary: Replace retry-only pnpm audit with one repository-owned OSV audit path and one independent CI job. Fetch and verify the scanner and current database under runner temp, scan both lockfiles offline, validate coverage and status/report consistency, then make default gates depend on the audit job.

policy.clean: Status 0, valid report, exact source coverage, nonempty package inventories, zero vulnerabilities, and no warnings passes.
policy.finding: Status 1 with at least one package carrying a nonempty vulnerabilities array fails.
policy.error: All other statuses or malformed, missing, inconsistent, stale, incomplete, or warning-bearing evidence fails.
policy.equivalence: This is a non-equivalent public OSV policy and intentionally fails on every OSV finding; it does not claim npm audit parity or private-registry coverage.
